title: When the Recipe Burns
premise: Ulyana Lockridge has spent twelve years keeping her head down in the small town of Bellhaven, channeling everything she can't say into her father's bakery, where she bakes grief into rye and longing into honey loaves. When her best friend Marisol vanishes days before graduation, leaving only a ring of keys and a half-finished letter, Ulyana discovers Marisol was investigating why the town's founding families—including Ulyana's own—profited from a decades-old fire that displaced half the immigrant quarter. Following the keys through locked rooms and buried ledgers, Ulyana must choose between protecting her family's reputation and telling the truth that could save Marisol, who is hiding in the ruins of the old mill. In the end, Ulyana testifies at the town hearing, loses her father's approval but keeps Marisol's fragile forgiveness, and bakes one last loaf—her own name kneaded into it—for the first time.
about_author: Petra Yarrow grew up above her grandmother's bakery in a rust-belt town where every family had a story they didn't tell. She writes young adult novels about quiet kids who discover that silence is also a choice with consequences.

chapters.title: The Careful Years
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. We meet her in the pre-dawn bakery, learning how she bakes emotions into bread for customers who never know what they're eating. Establishes her invisibility strategy at school and her closeness to Marisol, the only person who notices her. Emotional beat: comfort curdling into claustrophobia as graduation approaches.

chapters.title: Keys on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: Marisol misses their traditional Friday bake night, then three more days of school. Ulyana finds a ring of unlabeled keys and an unfinished letter on Marisol's windowsill, addressed to her, ending mid-sentence: 'If I don't come back, look at what your—'. Emotional beat: dread replacing irritation; the first crack in Ulyana's careful world.

chapters.title: What the Locks Open
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The first key opens the historical society's basement archive, where Ulyana finds photos of the 1979 mill fire and a list of families who bought burned-out lots cheap—including 'Lockridge.' Emotional beat: vertigo as her identity as the baker's careful daughter collides with being heir to something shameful.

chapters.title: Honey Loaf for Liars
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana POV with Marisol's hidden journal entries. Ulyana confronts her father gently; he shuts down, orders her to stop asking questions, and burns his own copy of the mill ledger in the bread oven. Emotional beat: love against duty—she watches him choose the family myth over her.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Kept Score
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Deshawn, whose grandmother lost her home in the fire, reveals he and Marisol were working together and that Marisol got scared when someone followed her. He distrusts Ulyana because of her last name. Emotional beat: the price of survival—Ulyana realizes her silence made her complicit in others' eyes.

chapters.title: Someone Follows Her Too
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A black truck tails her from the archive; she escapes by ducking into the bakery and lying to a councilman who comes asking about Marisol. That night she bakes panic into a sourdough and can't eat it. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; staying invisible is no longer possible or safe.

chapters.title: The Letter Finished
chapters.summary: Deshawn and Ulyana decode the rest of Marisol's letter using the remaining keys, discovering she found proof the fire was set for insurance money and that she's hiding in the old mill ruins. They race there at dawn. Emotional beat: rising terror and fierce loyalty; the friendship worth any cost.

chapters.title: Millstone
chapters.summary: Climax. In the collapsing mill, Ulyana finds Marisol injured and cornered by the councilman's son, who's been destroying evidence. Ulyana uses her knowledge of the building—the same building her grandfather bought—to get them out, then refuses a bribe to stay quiet. Emotional beat: courage; Ulyana finally speaks the truth aloud, loudly, publicly.

chapters.title: Testimony and Rye
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the town hearing, she reads the ledger aloud, implicating her own family. Her father walks out; her mother stays. Marisol, back but changed, watches from the back and doesn't defend her—but doesn't deny her either. Emotional beat: grief and liberation intertwined; truth costs exactly what it promised to.

chapters.title: Her Own Name in the Dough
chapters.summary: Resolution. Weeks later, Ulyana signs her first loaf of bread with scored dough, opens the bakery under a new honest sign, and shares a table with Marisol—not restored, but beginning again. Deshawn's grandmother gets the first slice. Emotional beat: identity claimed; survival redefined as living visibly, imperfectly, out loud.
